sanskrit: triṣu varṣeṣu pūrṇeṣu diptānalasamadyutim rūpaudāryaguṇopetaṃ dauḥṣantiṃ janamejaya
english: When three full years had passed, O Janamejaya, she bore Duḥṣanta's son, blazing with the splendour of a bright flame, endowed with beauty, noble bearing, and every virtue.

sanskrit: jātakarmādisaṃskāraṃ kaṇvaḥ puṇyakṛtāṃ varaḥ tasyātha kārayām āsa vardhamānasya dhīmataḥ
english: Kaṇva, foremost among the doers of righteous deeds, then caused the birth-rites and the other purificatory sacraments to be performed for that growing and wise child.

sanskrit: dantaiḥ śuklaiḥ śikharibhiḥ siṃhasaṃhanano yuvā cakrāṅkitakaraḥ śrīmān mahāmūrdhā mahābalaḥ kumāro devagarbhābhaḥ sa tatrāśu vyavardhata
english: With white, peak-like teeth, the frame of a lion, the mark of the wheel on his palm, majestic in bearing, with a great head and immense strength, a boy godlike in radiance — he swiftly grew up there.

sanskrit: ṣaḍvarṣa eva bālaḥ sa kaṇvāśramapadaṃ prati vyāghrān siṃhān varāhāṃś ca gajāṃś ca mahiṣāṃs tathā
english: Even as a boy of only six, around the precinct of Kaṇva's hermitage, he would seize tigers, lions, boars, elephants, and buffaloes —

sanskrit: baddhvā vṛkṣeṣu balavān āśramasya samantataḥ ārohan damayaṃś caiva krīḍaṃś ca paridhāvati
english: — binding them to trees on every side of the hermitage; the powerful boy would mount them, subdue them, and run about at play.

sanskrit: tato 'sya nāma cakrus te kaṇvāśramanivāsinaḥ astv ayaṃ sarvadamanaḥ sarvaṃ hi damayaty ayam
english: Then the inhabitants of Kaṇva's hermitage gave him his name: 'Let this boy be Sarvadamana — Tamer of All — for he tames everything.'

sanskrit: sa sarvadamano nāma kumāraḥ samapadyata vikrameṇaujasā caiva balena ca samanvitaḥ
english: So the prince came to bear the name Sarvadamana, endowed with heroic prowess, brilliant energy, and might.

sanskrit: taṃ kumāram ṛṣir dṛṣṭvā karma cāsyātimānuṣam samayo yauvarājyāyety abravīc ca śakuntalām
english: The sage, seeing the prince and his superhuman deeds, declared, 'The time has come for his installation as crown prince,' and so he told Śakuntalā.

sanskrit: tasya tad balam ājñāya kaṇvaḥ śiṣyān uvāca ha śakuntalām imāṃ śīghraṃ sahaputrām ito ''śramāt bhartre prāpayatādyaiva sarvalakṣaṇapūjitām
english: Recognising that strength, Kaṇva addressed his disciples: 'Lead this Śakuntalā today, without delay, together with her son, from this hermitage to her husband — she who is honoured by every auspicious mark.'

sanskrit: nārīṇāṃ ciravāso hi bāndhaveṣu na rocate kīrticāritradharmaghnas tasmān nayata māciram
english: For a woman's long sojourn among her kinsmen is not fitting; it destroys reputation, conduct, and righteousness. Therefore take her without further delay.

sanskrit: tathety uktvā tu te sarve prātiṣṭhantāmitaujasaḥ śakuntalāṃ puraskṛtya saputrāṃ gajasāhvayam
english: Saying 'So be it,' all of them, those of immeasurable energy, set out placing Śakuntalā together with her son at their head, bound for Hastinapura.

sanskrit: gṛhītvāmaragarbhābhaṃ putraṃ kamalalocanam ājagāma tataḥ śubhrā duḥṣantaviditād vanāt
english: Taking with her that lotus-eyed son, radiant as a child of the gods, the fair-complexioned Śakuntalā came forth from the forest that Duḥṣanta had known.

sanskrit: abhisṛtya ca rājānaṃ viditā sā praveśitā saha tenaiva putreṇa taruṇādityavarcasā
english: Having approached the king and been duly recognised, she was ushered into his presence together with that son of hers who shone with the lustre of the young sun.

sanskrit: pūjayitvā yathānyāyam abravīt taṃ śakuntalā ayaṃ putras tvayā rājan yauvarājye 'bhiṣicyatām
english: Having paid him reverence according to due form, Śakuntalā spoke to him: 'O king, let this son whom you fathered be consecrated as crown prince.'

sanskrit: tvayā hy ayaṃ suto rājan mayy utpannaḥ suropamaḥ yathāsamayam etasmin vartasva puruṣottama
english: For this son, O king, was begotten by you upon me, and he is equal to the gods. Act towards him according to the compact you made, O best of men.

sanskrit: yathā samāgame pūrvaṃ kṛtaḥ sa samayas tvayā taṃ smarasva mahābhāga kaṇvāśramapadaṃ prati
english: Recall, O greatly fortunate one, that compact which was earlier made by you at our meeting in the precinct of Kaṇva's hermitage.

sanskrit: so 'tha śrutvaiva tad vākyaṃ tasyā rājā smarann api abravīn na smarāmīti kasya tvaṃ duṣṭatāpasi
english: Having heard that speech of hers, the king — though he remembered — declared, 'I do not remember. Whose woman are you, O wicked ascetic?'

sanskrit: dharmakāmārthasaṃbandhaṃ na smarāmi tvayā saha gaccha vā tiṣṭha vā kāmaṃ yad vāpīcchasi tat kuru
english: 'I recall no connection with you in respect of righteousness, pleasure, or worldly gain. Go, or stay, as you please — do whatever you wish.'

sanskrit: saivam uktā varārohā vrīḍiteva manasvinī visaṃjñeva ca duḥkhena tasthau sthāṇur ivācalā
english: Thus addressed, that fair-hipped, proud-spirited woman stood as though shamed, almost insensible with grief, motionless as a post.

sanskrit: saṃrambhāmarṣatāmrākṣī sphuramāṇoṣṭhasaṃpuṭā kaṭākṣair nirdahantīva tiryag rājānam aikṣata
english: Her eyes red with fury and indignation, her lips quivering, she looked askance at the king as though burning him with her sideward glances.

sanskrit: ākāraṃ gūhamānā ca manyunābhisamīritā tapasā saṃbhṛtaṃ tejo dhārayām āsa vai tadā
english: Concealing her outward expression, stirred by wrath, she restrained at that moment the ascetic energy she had gathered through her austerities.

sanskrit: sā muhūrtam iva dhyātvā duḥkhāmarṣasamanvitā bhartāram abhisaṃprekṣya kruddhā vacanam abravīt
english: Having reflected for a moment, filled with grief and anger, and gazing steadily at her husband, she spoke these words in fury.

sanskrit: jānann api mahārāja kasmād evaṃ prabhāṣase na jānāmīti niḥsaṅgaṃ yathānyaḥ prākṛtas tathā
english: 'Though you know, O great king, why do you speak thus — "I do not know" — as indifferently as some common, ordinary man?'

sanskrit: atra te hṛdayaṃ veda satyasyaivānṛtasya ca kalyāṇa bata sākṣī tvaṃ mātmānam avamanyathāḥ
english: 'Your own heart knows the truth and the untruth here; O auspicious one — you yourself are the witness. Do not demean yourself.'

sanskrit: yo 'nyathā santam ātmānam anyathā pratipadyate kiṃ tena na kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ coreṇātmāpahāriṇā
english: 'One who, being otherwise, passes himself off as otherwise — what sin has not been committed by that self-thief, that robber of his own soul?'

sanskrit: eko 'ham asmīti ca manyase tvaṃ; na hṛcchayaṃ vetsi muniṃ purāṇam yo veditā karmaṇaḥ pāpakasya; tasyāntike tvaṃ vṛjinaṃ karoṣi
english: 'You think yourself alone — you do not know the ancient sage dwelling in the heart, who is the knower of every sinful deed; yet it is before him that you commit this wrong.'

sanskrit: manyate pāpakaṃ kṛtvā na kaś cid vetti mām iti vidanti cainaṃ devāś ca svaś caivāntarapūruṣaḥ
english: 'He who has done evil thinks "no one knows me," yet the gods know him, and so does the inner Person who dwells within him.'

sanskrit: ādityacandrāv anilānalau ca; dyaur bhūmir āpo hṛdayaṃ yamaś ca ahaś ca rātriś ca ubhe ca saṃdhye; dharmaś ca jānāti narasya vṛttam
english: 'The sun and the moon, wind and fire, sky, earth, water, the heart, Yama, day and night, and both twilights — and Dharma — all know a man's conduct.'

sanskrit: yamo vaivasvatas tasya niryātayati duṣkṛtam hṛdi sthitaḥ karmasākṣī kṣetrajño yasya tuṣyati
english: 'Yama Vaivasvata exacts the penalty for the evil deeds of that man with whose conduct the witness of deeds, the knower of the field, dwelling in the heart, is displeased.'

sanskrit: na tu tuṣyati yasyaiṣa puruṣasya durātmanaḥ taṃ yamaḥ pāpakarmāṇaṃ niryātayati duṣkṛtam
english: 'But of that wicked-souled man with whom this inner witness is not pleased, Yama exacts retribution for his evil deeds.'

sanskrit: avamanyātmanātmānam anyathā pratipadyate devā na tasya śreyāṃso yasyātmāpi na kāraṇam
english: 'One who demeans himself and behaves contrary to his own nature — the gods do not bestow their grace upon him for whom even his own self is no authority.'

sanskrit: svayaṃ prāpteti mām evaṃ māvamaṃsthāḥ pativratām arghyārhāṃ nārcayasi māṃ svayaṃ bhāryām upasthitām
english: 'Do not scorn me thus, thinking "she came of her own accord" — I, your faithful wife, I who deserve to be honoured, I who have come before you myself — you do not honour me.'

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ māṃ prākṛtavad upaprekṣasi saṃsadi na khalv aham idaṃ śūnye raumi kiṃ na śṛṇoṣi me
english: 'Why do you look upon me like a common man in this assembly? I am not saying this in private — do you not hear me?'

sanskrit: yadi me yācamānāyā vacanaṃ na kariṣyasi duḥṣanta śatadhā mūrdhā tatas te 'dya phaliṣyati
english: 'If you will not heed my plea, O Duḥṣanta, then this very day your head shall split into a hundred pieces.'

sanskrit: bhāryāṃ patiḥ saṃpraviśya sa yasmāj jāyate punaḥ jāyāyā iti jāyātvaṃ purāṇāḥ kavayo viduḥ
english: 'Because a husband enters his wife and is born again from her, the ancient sages know the wifeness of a wife as jāyā — she from whom he is born anew.'

sanskrit: yad āgamavataḥ puṃsas tad apatyaṃ prajāyate tat tārayati saṃtatyā pūrvapretān pitāmahān
english: 'The offspring that is born to a man comes from him — it delivers his lineage of deceased fathers and grandfathers who have gone before.'

sanskrit: pun nāmno narakād yasmāt pitaraṃ trāyate sutaḥ tasmāt putra iti proktaḥ svayam eva svayambhuvā
english: 'Because a son delivers his father from the hell called Put, the Self-existent One himself has called him putra — the deliverer.'

sanskrit: sā bhāryā yā gṛhe dakṣā sā bhāryā yā prajāvatī sā bhāryā yā patiprāṇā sā bhāryā yā pativratā
english: 'She is a true wife who is capable in the home; she is a true wife who bears children; she is a true wife whose life is her husband; she is a true wife who is devoted to her husband.'

sanskrit: ardhaṃ bhāryā manuṣyasya bhāryā śreṣṭhatamaḥ sakhā bhāryā mūlaṃ trivargasya bhāryā mitraṃ mariṣyataḥ
english: 'A wife is half of a man; a wife is his best companion; a wife is the root of the three aims of life; a wife is the friend of him who is to die.'

sanskrit: bhāryāvantaḥ kriyāvantaḥ sabhāryā gṛhamedhinaḥ bhāryāvantaḥ pramodante bhāryāvantaḥ śriyānvitāḥ
english: 'Those who have wives can perform rites; together with their wives they are true householders; those who have wives rejoice; those who have wives are endowed with prosperity.'

sanskrit: sakhāyaḥ pravivikteṣu bhavanty etāḥ priyaṃvadāḥ pitaro dharmakāryeṣu bhavanty ārtasya mātaraḥ
english: 'In solitary moments wives become sweet-spoken companions; in the duties of righteousness they become fathers; to one in distress they become mothers.'

sanskrit: kāntāreṣv api viśrāmo narasyādhvanikasya vai yaḥ sadāraḥ sa viśvāsyas tasmād dārāḥ parā gatiḥ
english: 'Even in the wilderness a wife is the resting-place for the wayfaring man. He who has a wife is trustworthy; therefore a wife is the highest refuge.'

sanskrit: saṃsarantam api pretaṃ viṣameṣv ekapātinam bhāryaivānveti bhartāraṃ satataṃ yā pativratā
english: 'Even the departed spirit wandering alone through difficult passages — a faithful wife ever follows her husband.'

sanskrit: prathamaṃ saṃsthitā bhāryā patiṃ pretya pratīkṣate pūrvaṃ mṛtaṃ ca bhartāraṃ paścāt sādhvy anugacchati
english: 'A wife who dies first waits for her husband after death; or if her husband dies first, the virtuous wife follows him afterwards.'

sanskrit: etasmāt kāraṇād rājan pāṇigrahaṇam iṣyate yad āpnoti patir bhāryām iha loke paratra ca
english: 'For this reason, O king, the taking of a wife's hand in marriage is prescribed — for what a husband obtains in his wife belongs to him both in this world and in the next.'

sanskrit: ātmātmanaiva janitaḥ putra ity ucyate budhaiḥ tasmād bhāryāṃ naraḥ paśyen mātṛvat putramātaram
english: 'The wise declare that a son is the self begotten by the self; therefore a man should regard his wife as the mother of his son, as he would regard his own mother.'

sanskrit: bhāryāyāṃ janitaṃ putram ādarśe svam ivānanam hlādate janitā preṣkya svargaṃ prāpyeva puṇyakṛt
english: 'A father, beholding the son born of his wife — like seeing his own face in a mirror — is gladdened, as if the meritorious man had attained heaven.'

sanskrit: dahyamānā manoduḥkhair vyādhibhiś cāturā narāḥ hlādante sveṣu dāreṣu gharmārtāḥ salileṣv iva
english: 'Men afflicted by the burnings of mental grief and by diseases find delight in their wives, as those tormented by the heat find relief in water.'

sanskrit: susaṃrabdho 'pi rāmāṇāṃ na brūyād apriyaṃ budhaḥ ratiṃ prītiṃ ca dharmaṃ ca tāsv āyattam avekṣya ca
english: 'Even in great anger a wise man should not speak harshly to women, seeing that pleasure, affection, and righteousness are all dependent upon them.'

sanskrit: ātmano janmanaḥ kṣetraṃ puṇyaṃ rāmāḥ sanātanam ṛṣīṇām api kā śaktiḥ sraṣṭuṃ rāmām ṛte prajāḥ
english: 'Women are the sacred, eternal field of one's own birth — what power would even the sages have to create offspring without a woman?'

sanskrit: paripatya yadā sūnur dharaṇīreṇuguṇṭhitaḥ pitur āśliṣyate 'ṅgāni kim ivāsty adhikaṃ tataḥ
english: 'When a son, who has been running about covered in the dust of the earth, runs up and embraces his father's limbs — what greater joy can there be than that?'

sanskrit: sa tvaṃ svayam anuprāptaṃ sābhilāṣam imaṃ sutam prekṣamāṇaṃ ca kākṣeṇa kimartham avamanyase
english: 'Why then do you disdain this very son who has come to you of himself, who longs for you, and who looks at you with expectant eyes?'

sanskrit: aṇḍāni bibhrati svāni na bhindanti pipīlikāḥ na bharethāḥ kathaṃ nu tvaṃ dharmajñaḥ san svam ātmajam
english: 'Even ants carry their own eggs and do not break them — how then, knowing righteousness as you do, could you not support your own son?'

sanskrit: na vāsasāṃ na rāmāṇāṃ nāpāṃ sparśas tathā sukhaḥ śiśor āliṅgyamānasya sparśaḥ sūnor yathā sukhaḥ
english: 'The touch of garments, of women, or of water is not as pleasurable as the touch of a small child being embraced — the touch of one's own son.'

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo dvipadāṃ śreṣṭho gaur variṣṭhā catuṣpadām gurur garīyasāṃ śreṣṭhaḥ putraḥ sparśavatāṃ varaḥ
english: 'A brahmin is the foremost among two-footed beings; the cow is the greatest among four-footed beings; a teacher is the best among elders; a son is the most excellent of all things that can be touched.'

sanskrit: spṛśatu tvāṃ samāśliṣya putro 'yaṃ priyadarśanaḥ putrasparśāt sukhataraḥ sparśo loke na vidyate
english: 'Let this comely son embrace you and touch you — there is no more pleasurable touch in the world than the touch of a son.'

sanskrit: triṣu varṣeṣu pūrṇeṣu prajātāham ariṃdama imaṃ kumāraṃ rājendra tava śokapraṇāśanam
english: 'Three full years after I gave birth, O subduer of foes, O lord of kings — I bring you this prince who will put an end to your sorrows.'

sanskrit: āhartā vājimedhasya śatasaṃkhyasya paurava iti vāg antarikṣe māṃ sūtake 'bhyavadat purā
english: 'O Paurava, a voice from the sky once addressed me at his birth, saying he shall be the performer of a hundred horse-sacrifices.'

sanskrit: nanu nāmāṅkam āropya snehād grāmāntaraṃ gatāḥ mūrdhni putrān upāghrāya pratinandanti mānavāḥ
english: 'Do not men, even when travelling to another village, having first inhaled the fragrance of their sons' heads and marked them with a name-sign out of affection, bid them farewell with blessings?'

sanskrit: vedeṣv api vadantīmaṃ mantravādaṃ dvijātayaḥ jātakarmaṇi putrāṇāṃ tavāpi viditaṃ tathā
english: 'The twice-born recite this Vedic declaration at the birth-rite of sons — you too know it likewise:'

sanskrit: aṅgād aṅgāt saṃbhavasi hṛdayād abhijāyase ātmā vai putranāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śatam
english: '"You are born from limb after limb, you spring forth from the heart; you are the self who bears the name of son — so live a hundred autumns."'

sanskrit: poṣo hi tvadadhīno me saṃtānam api cākṣayam tasmāt tvaṃ jīva me vatsa susukhī śaradāṃ śatam
english: 'My sustenance and my undying lineage depend upon you — therefore, live happily a hundred autumns, my dear child.'

sanskrit: tvadaṅgebhyaḥ prasūto 'yaṃ puruṣāt puruṣo 'paraḥ sarasīvāmale ''tmānaṃ dvitīyaṃ paśya me sutam
english: 'This second man born from a man — born from your limbs — behold your own self as if reflected in a spotless pool, O king; behold my son.'

sanskrit: yathā hy āhavanīyo 'gnir gārhapatyāt praṇīyate tathā tvattaḥ prasūto 'yaṃ tvam ekaḥ san dvidhā kṛtaḥ
english: 'Just as the Āhavanīya fire is kindled from the Gārhapatya, so has this son been born from you — you being one, you are made twofold.'

sanskrit: mṛgāpakṛṣṭena hi te mṛgayāṃ paridhāvatā aham āsāditā rājan kumārī pitur āśrame
english: 'For it was you, pursuing game, drawn away by a deer, who found me, a maiden, in my father's hermitage while ranging in the hunt, O king.'

sanskrit: urvaśī pūrvacittiś ca sahajanyā ca menakā viśvācī ca ghṛtācī ca ṣaḍ evāpsarasāṃ varāḥ
english: 'Urvaśī, Pūrvacitti, Sahajanyā, Menakā, Viśvācī, and Ghṛtācī — these six are the foremost of the Apsarases.'

sanskrit: tāsāṃ māṃ menakā nāma brahmayonir varāpsarāḥ divaḥ saṃprāpya jagatīṃ viśvāmitrād ajījanat
english: 'Among them, Menakā by name, the foremost Apsaras sprung from Brahmā's creative power, descending from heaven to earth, bore me by Viśvāmitra.'

sanskrit: sā māṃ himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe suṣuve menakāpsarāḥ avakīrya ca māṃ yātā parātmajam ivāsatī
english: 'That Apsaras Menakā gave birth to me on the slopes of the Himālaya, and having abandoned me there she departed — like a wicked woman casting aside another's child.'

sanskrit: kiṃ nu karmāśubhaṃ pūrvaṃ kṛtavaty asmi janmani yad ahaṃ bāndhavais tyaktā bālye saṃprati ca tvayā
english: 'What inauspicious deed did I commit in a former birth, that I was abandoned by my kin in childhood and now again by you?'

sanskrit: kāmaṃ tvayā parityaktā gamiṣyāmy aham āśramam imaṃ tu bālaṃ saṃtyaktuṃ nārhasy ātmajam ātmanā
english: 'Abandoned by you I shall willingly go back to the hermitage — but you should not abandon this child, your own son born of yourself.'

sanskrit: duḥṣanta uvāca na putram abhijānāmi tvayi jātaṃ śakuntale asatyavacanā nāryaḥ kas te śraddhāsyate vacaḥ
english: Duḥṣanta spoke: 'I do not acknowledge a son born of you, O Śakuntalā. Women are untruthful in their speech — who would trust your words?'

sanskrit: menakā niranukrośā bandhakī jananī tava yayā himavataḥ pṛṣṭhe nirmālyeva praveritā
english: 'Your mother Menakā is a merciless harlot — she who cast you away on the slopes of the Himālaya like a discarded garland.'

sanskrit: sa cāpi niranukrośaḥ kṣatrayoniḥ pitā tava viśvāmitro brāhmaṇatve lubdhaḥ kāmaparāyaṇaḥ
english: 'And that merciless father of yours, Viśvāmitra — born of kṣatriya stock, greedy for brahminhood, entirely given over to lust.'

sanskrit: menakāpsarasāṃ śreṣṭhā maharṣīṇāṃ ca te pitā tayor apatyaṃ kasmāt tvaṃ puṃścalīvābhidhāsyasi
english: 'Menakā is the best of Apsarases and your father is a great sage — the offspring of those two — yet why do you present yourself like a wanton woman?'

sanskrit: aśraddheyam idaṃ vākyaṃ kathayantī na lajjase viśeṣato matsakāśe duṣṭatāpasi gamyatām
english: 'Are you not ashamed to speak these unbelievable words, especially in my presence? Go away, O wicked ascetic woman.'

sanskrit: kva maharṣiḥ sadaivograḥ sāpsarā kva ca menakā kva ca tvam evaṃ kṛpaṇā tāpasīveṣadhāriṇī
english: 'Where stands the great sage, ever terrible, and where the Apsaras Menakā — and where do you stand, so pitiable, wearing the mere garb of an ascetic woman?'

sanskrit: atikāyaś ca putras te bālo 'pi balavān ayam katham alpena kālena śālaskandha ivodgataḥ
english: 'And this son of yours is huge, and even as a child immensely strong — how has he grown up in such a short time, like the trunk of a śāla tree?'

sanskrit: sunikṛṣṭā ca yonis te puṃścalī pratibhāsi me yadṛcchayā kāmarāgāj jātā menakayā hy asi
english: 'Your origin is very low — you appear to me a wanton woman; for you were born of Menakā by random desire and lust.'

sanskrit: sarvam etat parokṣaṃ me yat tvaṃ vadasi tāpasi nāhaṃ tvām abhijānāmi yatheṣṭaṃ gamyatāṃ tvayā
english: 'All that you say, O ascetic woman, is unknown to me. I do not recognise you. Go wherever you please.'

sanskrit: śakuntalovāca rājan sarṣapamātrāṇi paracchidrāṇi paśyasi ātmano bilvamātrāṇi paśyann api na paśyasi
english: Śakuntalā spoke: 'O king, you see the faults of others though they be but the size of a mustard seed, yet even when you behold your own faults, though they be the size of a bilva fruit, you do not see them.'
